note: The everyday Talk-to conversation, opened when the follower has asked nothing. Kept apart from dialogs.json because it does not change with play - it is what the follower is, not what it is currently up to; the trees in dialogs.json are the ones the follower OPENS, which is a different job. Bundled only, never copied out or edited in game. Three rules hold this together. Every choice leads to a node where the PLAYER says that exact line: the game works that way and players read it that way - the option is the sentence you are about to speak, not a summary of it. Jumping straight to a menu instead reads as the click having gone astray, and an option whose node says something slightly different reads as a bug, because it is one. A test enforces the match. Nothing here is a feature list: what the follower can do comes out as habits and grievances, the way a person describes their job, because a companion reciting its own capabilities is a manual with a face. And a branch never replays a line already read - hence the -menu nodes, which re-offer the follow-ups without the preamble. A node with "when" is built only while every fact it names holds, and a fact with ! only while it does not: wish (a wish is open), held (it is, and the wished thing is in the bag), lowish (the mood band is low or down), the band itself (low, down, even, good, high), and likes, errands and thrall-outfits (the build has them). Of the nodes sharing an id exactly one is built, in its place in the list. {wish} is the wished thing. moods: what the day summary says of each mood band; any other band gets the ordinary one.

nodes.note: The gift option only exists while a wish is open, and it names the thing, because the first design taught us the failure the hard way: "Found you something" with no something reads as a null action, and giving with no wanting before it has no pull. The follower asks for a feather; the option is "Found you that feather."; everything downstream says feather. The script is rebuilt on every Talk-to, so the option appears and disappears with the wish. When the follower is not itself, "How have you been?" sharpens into "You all right?" - same slot, same spirit, pointed by state. The research calls this answering its mood, and it is the one thing a player can DO about a low band besides witness it. While a wish is open the five-slot box retires who-are-you, not the small talk: who-a stays reachable from the returning hub later, but the jokes and advice are the perishable first-hour charm, and a 45-minute wish window used to wall them off from the opening screen.

nodes.note: The gift. Client-side, so nothing real changes hands: the box closes on the handover and the verdict arrives overhead from the gifted-* rules, the shape the hands game uses - fixed text here, consequence from the rules. The box branches on the bag, because the first neutral version ("Let's see it, then." either way) read as the follower not looking - and a scribe that does not look is out of character in its own conversation. The bag is read when the script is built; the rules re-check at dispatch, so the rare mid-box drop still gets an honest overhead answer.

Second page, and it earns its click: nothing is consumed, so the player walks away still holding the thing they just handed over, and a handover that leaves the bag untouched reads as the gift not having registered. The follower trading its worn one back is the honest account of what the bag will show - the count does not move because a swap does not move it - and it is truer to a scribe than pretending to pocket something it cannot pocket.
says: Let's see it, then. ...That's the one.

nodes.note: The one page in the script that is different every time it is read. Everything in it is already counted - the tallies exist for the milestone lines - so this is the same memory said as a sentence rather than as a number, which is what makes it sound like somebody who was there rather than a scoreboard. how-today-a's pages are that summary, built on each visit.

When it's gone well I stand one way. When it hasn't, I stand another.
